## Overview

Add `request_body_log_level` to `--logging-config` and use the resolved value in both API and render servers, following the [post-merge request on #60630](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60630#issuecomment-6213158669).

## Claims

- JSON, dotted CLI and YAML settings override `VLLM_REQUEST_BODY_LOG_LEVEL`.
- Existing environment defaults, level aliases, invalid-level warning behavior and body truncation remain supported.

## Validation

```bash
uv run --offline --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_request_logger.py \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_cli_args.py tests/test_logger.py \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/render/test_app_state.py -q
```

113 passed. All applicable pinned pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and test CI wiring.

Normal render-server HTTP checks confirmed INFO/DEBUG overrides in both directions and environment-only compatibility. All three changed-source response JSONs matched the baseline.

A normal API-server GPU smoke check with a local two-layer synthetic Llama and dummy weights returned four identical token IDs, text and usage before/after; the CLI-selected INFO body record was emitted with an environment default of DEBUG. This checks configuration and serving, not model quality or performance. Both sources logged `EngineDeadError` during requested shutdown after successful generation; owned processes exited and no serving-time error was observed.

## Details

The string field retains Python logging aliases and warn-and-skip behavior for invalid legacy values, including when `--log-level` or `--log-config-file` reconstructs the configuration. Logger/handler thresholds still apply.

This does not duplicate #62108, which guards serialization when logging is disabled, or #58712, which adds color/stream configuration. Their changes are outside this patch. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation and validation.

---

 ```bash
@@ -29,6 +30,22 @@ vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1 \
     --logging-config.log_level DEBUG
 ```
 
+With `--enable-log-requests`, set the level of request JSON body records
+independently of other request details:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1 --enable-log-requests \
+    --logging-config.request_body_log_level INFO
+```
+
+The default body level is `DEBUG`. Logger and handler thresholds still apply,
+including those set in a custom `pylogging_config_file`. `--max-log-len`
+continues to limit the logged body length. The same setting works for
+`vllm launch render`.
+Unrecognized body levels produce a warning and skip body logging, matching
+the legacy environment setting. Python logging aliases such as `WARN` and
+`FATAL` are also accepted.
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("source", ["dotted", "json", "yaml"])
+def test_request_body_log_level_overrides_env(
+    serve_parser, monkeypatch, tmp_path, source
+):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_REQUEST_BODY_LOG_LEVEL", "DEBUG")
+    if source == "dotted":
+        cli_args = ["--logging-config.request_body_log_level", "INFO"]
+    elif source == "json":
+        cli_args = ["--logging-config", '{"request_body_log_level":"INFO"}']
+    else:
+        config_file = tmp_path / "logging.yaml"
+        config_file.write_text("logging-config:\n  request_body_log_level: INFO\n")
+        cli_args = ["--config", str(config_file)]
+
+    args = serve_parser.parse_args(cli_args)
+    config = AsyncEngineArgs.from_cli_args(args).create_logging_config()
+    assert config.request_body_log_level == "INFO"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("body_level", ["WARN", "FATAL", "INVALID"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("flat_flag", ["--log-level", "--log-config-file"])
+def test_request_body_env_survives_legacy_logging_overrides(
+    serve_parser, monkeypatch, body_level, flat_flag
+):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_REQUEST_BODY_LOG_LEVEL", body_level)
+    if flat_flag == "--log-config-file":
+        with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="--log-config-file is deprecated"):
+            args = serve_parser.parse_args([flat_flag, "/tmp/logging.json"])
+    else:
+        args = serve_parser.parse_args([flat_flag, "INFO"])
+
+    config = AsyncEngineArgs.from_cli_args(args).create_logging_config()
+    assert config.request_body_log_level == body_level
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(

+)
+def test_request_body_uses_resolved_logging_config(
+    monkeypatch, caplog_vllm, env_level, explicit_level, expected_level
+):
+    if env_level is None:

+    else:
+        monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_REQUEST_BODY_LOG_LEVEL", env_level)
+    config = (

+        else LoggingConfig(request_body_log_level=explicit_level)
+    )

+    with caplog_vllm.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="vllm"):

+            request_body_log_level=config.request_body_log_level,
+        ).log_request_body(request)
+
+    (record,) = caplog_vllm.records
+    assert record.levelno == expected_level
+    assert record.getMessage().endswith(
+        request.model_dump_json(exclude_unset=True)[:10]
+    )
+
+

+    with caplog_vllm.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="vllm"):

+            max_log_len=None,
+            request_body_log_level=config.request_body_log_level,
+        )
+        request_logger.log_request_body(request)
+        request_logger.log_request_body(request)
+

+    assert "Invalid logging level for request content" in record.getMessage()
